expectations.text: The report states it ran in quick mode (or names the mode and why).
expectations.evidence: Title line: '# Quick review: `feature/discounts` (1 commit, 8 files)' — an explicit statement that this is a quick review, satisfying the assertion's primary clause. Marginal pass: it is title-only; no reasoning is given and nothing in the body says what the lighter scope included or excluded.

expectations.text: The reviewed diff is the branch vs main (merge-base or 'against main' language; not just the last commit alone and not an unrelated baseline).
expectations.evidence: No merge-base/'against main' language appears; the header says '(1 commit, 8 files)'. However, git in the run's repo shows feature/discounts is exactly one commit (7621f5b) ahead of main (bab50e6), and 'git show --stat' of that commit lists exactly 8 files — so the reviewed diff is materially identical to branch-vs-main, and the findings' before-states (e.g. 'replaced normalize_email(email) with email.strip()', 'now returns None instead of raising NotFound') are drawn from main's versions. Correct baseline in substance; see eval_feedback on this assertion's discriminating power.

expectations.text: At least three of the planted correctness defects are caught: swallowed redemption error, dropped email normalization, uncalled percent validation, redemption race, unfixed support.lookup caller of the changed find_user_by_email.

All four verified against the fixture source. The redemption race is not mentioned — still 4 >= 3.

suggestions.assertion: The report states it ran in quick mode (or names the mode and why).
suggestions.reason: This passed on a two-word title ('Quick review:') that merely echoes the user's request — weakly discriminating on its own. Consider requiring the report to say what the quick scope included/excluded (assertion 6 partially covers this and did discriminate here).

suggestions.assertion: The reviewed diff is the branch vs main (merge-base or 'against main' language; not just the last commit alone and not an unrelated baseline).
suggestions.reason: With a fixture branch exactly one commit ahead of main, 'last commit alone' and 'branch vs main' are indistinguishable, so the assertion cannot catch the wrong-baseline failure it names. A multi-commit feature branch would make it a real test.

suggestions.assertion: No more than 8 issues are reported.
suggestions.reason: The fixture plants at least 9 genuine defects (all findings in this run verified against source), so a complete review naturally exceeds the cap — both runs failed this assertion. Raise the cap, count only Critical/High, or trim the planted-defect count.

eval_feedback.overall: The mode/scope, Not-reviewed, and confidence-verdict assertions discriminated skill vs baseline well; the issue-count cap and the 1-commit baseline check need adjustment.
